sentences.text: The small-billed moa-nalo was an extinct, flightless bird resembling a goose-like duck.
Like the genus Thambetochen, this species possessed bony, tooth-like projections on its jaws.
Its beak was proportionately shorter and deeper compared to other moa-nalo relatives.
The skull featured a more rounded cranium and lacked impressions of salt glands.
Remains were found exclusively at altitudes above 1100 meters on Haleakalā.
Fossils were discovered ranging from 1145 meters at Auwahi Cave to 1860 meters in the upper Kipahulu Valley.
The species was described in 1991 by Storrs Olson and Helen James based on material collected in September 1982.
Fossils were found at Auwahi Cave on the southern slopes of Haleakalā on the island of Maui.
The species belongs to the family Anatidae.
The species lived during the Holocene epoch, from 0.0117 million years ago until 0 million years ago.
